raw_response:
I have worked this land for 35 years. I know what works here in Quzhou. The soil is not rich — it needs feeding. Water comes from the well, so I have to plan carefully how many times I pump. My son and daughter-in-law go to the city for work, so I cannot do everything, but I manage.

Cotton is my main income. I put most land into it — about 9 mu. I will use the improved hybrid seed from the county seed shop, same as last few years. It handles the bollworm better. I plough deeply before planting, in April, and irrigate four times through the summer. Pesticide I spray five times — I watch the plants, especially in July when the aphids and bollworm are worst.

My other 5 mu I rotate wheat and maize. Wheat goes in October, harvested June. After I harvest the wheat I plant maize directly into the stubble without tilling — saves time and my back, and the village neighbors do it this way now. Maize is harvested in September.

The remaining 2.9 mu I plant mungbean in early summer. It does not need much. I save seeds from last year. It sells well at the local market and the family eats it too.
